Angela: A wonderful life by Angela D'Audney and Nicky Pellegrino
"Angela D’Audney wasn’t just reading the news — she was making history while doing it. A trailblazing New Zealand television news anchor and occasional actress, Angela earned the title of the country’s “first lady of broadcasting” and, in 1973, shattered the glass ceiling by becoming the first woman to regularly anchor nationwide news bulletins on New Zealand television."

Handiwoman by Len Elliott
"With a cover that epitomizes the 70s ... we all had Farrah Fawcett haircuts and were learning to take control of the little things - like how to fix things around the house."

New Zealand's World Cup by John Adshead and Kevin Fallon
"The cover embodies the excitement generated by the New Zealand football team’s (i.e. the All Whites) first appearance at a FIFA World Cup tournament in 1982. For a fanatical rugby nation it was extraordinary how so many New Zealanders came to get behind the All Whites. The shorts were noticeably shorter back in the 1980s!"

The Queer and the Rare Fishes of New Zealand by Arthur W. Parrott
"This book is all about contrasts, from the bright cover to the author and his subject matter and of course the use of words and their meanings today."
